IRS990.ActivityOrMissionDesc: Encourage and support state policymakers to improve availability & use of quality educational data.
IRS990.MissionDesc: The Data Quality Campaign is a national, nonprofit organization leading the effort to bring every part of the education community together to empower educators, parents, and policymakers with quality information to make decisions that ensure students achieve their best.
IRS990.Desc: The Data Quality Campaign (DQC) is a national nonprofit, nonpartisan advocacy organization launched in 2005 by 10 national organizations. DQC is based in Washington, DC and works at the national, state, and community levels. When students, parents, educators and policy makers have the right information to make decisions, students achieve their best. DQC is leading the national effort to make this vision a reality by working in a broad-based coalitions to ensure that people have the high-quality education data they need and the tools and conditions to use it to help students succeed in schools and beyond. DQC's Goal are: - Increase public understanding of the value of educational data. - ensure everyone with a stake in education has timely access to the information needed to support students success. - improve the capacity of and conditions for teachers and school leaders to use data to support student learning.

SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: We engaged in limited direct lobbying in support of our exempt purpose of improving data quality in education. During the year, staff devoted a small portion of their time to communicating with federal legislative staff regarding proposed legislation and budget provisions. These contacts consisted of occasional meetings and calls to provide nontechnical policy input and respond to information requests; no grassroots lobbying campaigns or mass communications to the general public were conducted. All lobbying activities were an insubstantial part of the organization's overall operations.
The board designated funds are intended for use in operations and program activities.

DQC evaluates uncertainty in income tax positions based on a more-likely-than-not recognition standard. If that threshold is met, the tax position is then measured at the largest amount that is greater than 50% likely of being realized upon ultimate settlement. As of June 30, 2025 and 2024, there are no accruals for uncertain tax positions. If applicable, DQC records interest and penalties as a component of income tax expense. Tax years from 2022 through the current year remain open for examination by tax authorities.
The organization provided bonus compensation to its employees during the fiscal year.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Section B, line 11b
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: A copy of Form 990 is reviewed by the audit and finance committee, and then by the full board of directors before being filed with the IRS.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Section B, line 12c
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: The board of directors holds two board meetings every year. On an annual basis at the first meeting every member of the board is required to complete a conflict-of-interest form; any conflicts, should they exist, are handled on an individual basis.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Section B, line 15
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: DQC has an independent compensation subcommittee of the board who reviews and approves the compensation of the president, executive directors, and the other top management officials. An outside consulting firm provides a compensation analysis for the deliberation process; the deliberation process is documented by the subcommittee.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Section C, line 19
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: Governing documents and financial statements are available to the public upon reasonable request.
